title: AtRial CArdiomyopathy - prevaleNce And clinical impact
summary:
The ARCANA study is a prospective, non-interventional observational study. Its aim is to improve the understanding of structural and functional changes of the atria, summarized under the term atrial cardiomyopathy (AtCM), and to investigate whether specific markers are associated with an increased risk of major clinical events such as stroke, newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation, or death.
Scientific evidence suggests that structural and functional alterations of the atria may be linked to a higher risk of stroke. In particular, in patients with embolic stroke of undetermined source (ESUS), previously unrecognized atrial abnormalities are suspected to represent a potential underlying mechanism. A more precise characterization of these atrial changes may help to better identify high-risk individuals and improve future prevention strategies.
The study includes adult participants aged 18 years or older who are able to provide informed consent. Three groups will be investigated:
a) Patients with a recent embolic stroke of undetermined source (ESUS),
b) Patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation,
c) Control participants without known structural heart disease, without atrial fibrillation, and without prior stroke.

All participants will continue to receive standard guideline-based medical care independent of the study.
In addition to routine clinical care, non-invasive examinations will be performed: a standard 12-lead ECG, a transthoracic echocardiography with special focus on atrial function, and additional blood samples taken during clinically indicated blood draws. The additional time required for these procedures is approximately 20–30 minutes. Furthermore, participants will be contacted once per year for five years for a brief telephone follow-up (approximately 5–10 minutes) to collect information on survival and the occurrence of stroke, transient ischemic attacks, or newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation.

This is not an interventional study. No experimental treatments will be administered, no randomization will take place, and no ionizing radiation will be used. The additional study-related procedures are low risk and do not substantially increase risk compared to routine medical care.

The ARCANA study aims to improve the understanding of atrial cardiomyopathy and to enable a more precise assessment of individual stroke and mortality risk in the future.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Patients with ESUS

Inclusion criteria

Diagnosis of ESUS:

Imaging-confirmed non-lacunar ischemic cerebral infarction

No ≥50% stenosis in an intra- or extracranial artery supplying the infarct territory

No evidence of a major cardioembolic source (e.g., atrial fibrillation)

No indication of other specific causes of stroke (e.g., arterial dissection, vasculitis)

Sinus rhythm at the time of study inclusion

Study inclusion within 30 days after the index event

Age ≥18 years and <90 years

Life expectancy >1 year

Written informed consent for study participation

2) Patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (clinically manifest AtCM)

Inclusion criteria

Confirmed diagnosis of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation according to ESC guidelines

Sinus rhythm at the time of study-related examinations

No prior stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA)

Planned or recently performed (≤30 days) rhythm intervention (e.g., electrical cardioversion, pulmonary vein isolation) or elective cardiology consultation

Age ≥18 years and <90 years

Life expectancy >1 year

Written informed consent for study participation

3) Control participants without manifest heart disease

Inclusion criteria

No known structural heart disease

No atrial fibrillation or other clinically relevant cardiac arrhythmias

No history of ischemic stroke or TIA

Sinus rhythm at the time of study inclusion

Age ≥18 years and <90 years

Life expectancy >1 year

Written informed consent for study participation
Exclusion criteria:
ESUS – Exclusion criteria

Occurrence of atrial fibrillation before or during the index hospitalization

Evidence of structural heart disease (e.g., severe valvular disease, severe left ventricular dysfunction <30%)

Advanced renal failure (GFR <15 ml/min)

Severe hepatic insufficiency

Overt hyperthyroidism

Prior heart valve replacement or coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery

Continuous pacemaker stimulation

AtCM (paroxysmal atrial fibrillation group) – Exclusion criteria

Persistent or long-standing atrial fibrillation without documented sinus rhythm

Structural heart disease (e.g., severe valvular disease, severe left ventricular dysfunction <30%)

Severe renal or hepatic insufficiency

Overt hyperthyroidism

Continuous pacemaker stimulation

History of prior stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA)

Control group – Exclusion criteria

Evidence of structural or functional heart disease

Suspicion of previously undiagnosed arrhythmias (e.g., AV block, supraventricular tachycardia)

History of stroke or TIA

Severe renal or hepatic insufficiency

Overt hyperthyroidism

Continuous pacemaker stimulation

General exclusion criteria (applicable to all groups)

Age <18 or ≥90 years

Life expectancy <1 year

Inability to provide informed consent

Refusal to participate in the study

Participation in another clinical study with potential influence on the study endpoints
